stories.title: Vicky the Volcano and the Hot Earth
learning_objectives: Volcanoes are openings in Earth’s surface
Hot melted rock is called magma or lava
Some volcanoes are active, others are quiet
Volcanoes can build new land
People study volcanoes to stay safe

pages.text: Deep inside the ground, the Earth feels warm. Vicky the volcano rests quietly above it.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel illustration of a calm volcano with gentle warm glow beneath the ground, kid-friendly and safe tone. 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: A volcano is an opening in the Earth. It connects the hot inside to the land above.

pages.text: Far below, rock melts from heat. Melted rock under the ground is called magma.

pages.text: When magma reaches the surface, it is called lava. Lava flows slowly and cools over time.

pages.text: Some volcanoes erupt often. Others stay quiet for a very long time.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel illustration comparing active and quiet volcanoes side by side, simple contrast. 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: As lava cools, it hardens into new rock. Volcanoes can slowly build new land.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel illustration showing lava cooling into land, positive creation theme. 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: People do not live very close when volcanoes are active. Safety is important.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel illustration of volcano with safe distance markers and small homes far away, reassuring tone. 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: Scientists watch volcanoes carefully. They study heat, movement, and gas.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel illustration of scientists observing volcano with instruments, friendly and calm. 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: Vicky reminds us: the Earth is alive inside, slowly changing the land we see.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel illustration of volcano connected to glowing Earth core, gentle wonder tone. 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: At bedtime, we remember: volcanoes show Earth’s heat and help shape new land.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel bedtime volcano scene under stars, calm and cozy mood. 1:1 aspect ratio.

stories.title: Wally the Weather Map and the Moving Sky
learning_objectives: Weather describes what the sky and air are like
Weather can change from day to day
Rain, wind, sun, and snow are types of weather
Weather maps help show weather in different places
Weather affects how people dress and plan

pages.text: Cold weather can turn rain into snow. Tiny ice pieces fall softly to the ground.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel illustration of snowflakes falling gently, calm winter feel. 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: Wally shows weather on a map. Symbols help us see what the weather is like in many places.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel illustration of weather map with simple symbols for sun, rain, snow across regions. 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: People check the weather to choose clothes and plan their day.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel illustration of children choosing raincoat, jacket, or hat based on weather, friendly tone. 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: Farmers, pilots, and sailors all use weather maps to stay safe.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel illustration of farmer, pilot, and sailor with weather symbols, simple and inclusive. 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: At bedtime, we remember: weather changes often, and maps help us understand the sky.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel bedtime scene with calm sky and weather map fading softly, cozy and reassuring. 1:1 aspect ratio.

stories.title: Mia the Map and Finding Places
learning_objectives: Maps show places from above
Maps help us find where things are
Maps use symbols to show roads, water, and buildings
Directions help us move from one place to another
Maps can show real places like towns and parks

pages.text: On the table lies Mia the map. She shows a town from above, like a bird looking down.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel illustration of a friendly map character showing a small town from a top-down view, kid-friendly, simple shapes. 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: Tiny pictures fill the map. Roads, houses, and parks are drawn in clear shapes.

pages.text: Mia does not show every detail. Maps keep things simple so places are easy to find.

pages.text: Directions guide the way. Left, right, forward, and back help us move safely.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel illustration of arrows on a map showing directions, simple and clear. 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: Maps can be small or big. Some show one park, others show whole cities.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel illustration comparing small map and large map side by side, simple scale idea. 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: Emergency helpers use maps too. Maps help them reach people faster.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel illustration of ambulance and fire truck following a map route, calm and reassuring. 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: With Mia, places make sense. We learn where we are and where we want to go.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel illustration of child happily tracing route on map, confidence-building tone. 1:1 aspect ratio.
